review_candidates.title: Regional Economic Development, Strategy & Coordination, and Engagement (Various Roles)
review_candidates.description: Desirable Location We are seeking to recruit people who currently reside in our priority regions, noting that in the Latrobe, Collie and Central Queensland these would be a 100% remote working arrangement (work from home). We currently have offices in Canberra and Sydney, and in the Hunter, there is a small Newcastle presence. However, consideration based on location will determine whether the role will be remote or whether there is an expectation to work some days in the office. About the Division The Regional Transformation Division supports the Authority's mission to ensure workers, industries and communities benefit from Australia's transition to a net zero economy. Through a place-based approach, the Authority focuses on four of Australia's key transition regions, the Hunter, Latrobe-Gippsland, Collie and Central Queensland, to foster partnerships and mobilise actions that support sustainable economic and workforce outcomes. As part of this, the Division also works to ensure First Nations peoples and communities are active participants in, and beneficiaries of, the opportunities created by the transition. There are four regions’ teams - Hunter, Latrobe-Gippsland, Collie and Central Queensland. Each team leads strategy and advice and coordinates engagement in one priority region. This includes identifying transition challenges and opportunities and working with government, non-government and community stakeholders to facilitate access to opportunities and delivery of associated supports. About the Roles The Division are looking to fill multiple roles at the APS 5, APS 6 and Executive Level 1 classifications. Executive Level 1 (Assistant Director) roles We are looking to fill a number of Assistant Director roles across the Division, who will lead workstreams within Regional Economic Development, Strategy and Coordination, and Engagement. These roles provide a unique opportunity to contribute to a key Australian Government priority by supporting economic transformation and growth, with a particular focus on opportunities arising from Australia’s energy transition and evolving energy policy landscape. APS 5 and APS 6 roles As a Regional Economic Development Officer, you will work closely with Assistant Directors to support the delivery of key projects relevant to the specific team/region. These roles will represent the Authority in the specific region. They will support Authority objectives under the Authority’s Business Plan, especially through strong policy, research and economic development skills. You will bring strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to navigate complex issues in a dynamic operating environment. Our Ideal Candidates We are seeking strongly motivated and collaborative professionals who are passionate about supporting regional communities through Australia’s net zero transformation and working on the challenges facing regional workers and communities. They will have a policy and economic background to support the team’s objectives to drive industry and job growth whilst supporting workforce transitioning away from coal industries. Ideal candidates will have strategic policy skills, including familiarity with Government systems and processes, and have interest in net zero, energy systems, economic development, industry and jobs growth, place-based policy and/or workforce support. Ideal candidates will also understand Commonwealth policy particularly how it relates to supporting industry and jobs growth in NZEA priority regions. For further details on the Teams in the Division and roles, including the specific duties, capabilities and behaviours to tailor your resume and pitch towards putting your best foot forward, please click the 'Apply Now' button to take you to the Authority's career page to the downloadable Candidate Information Pack.

Bij de Anne Frank Stichting werken ongeveer 250 medewerkers. De stichting brengt haar levensverhaal en haar werk wereldwijd onder de aandacht, mede ter bezinning op de gevaren van antisemitisme, racisme en discriminatie en het belang van vrijheid, gelijke rechten en democratie. Projectassistent Jongerenprogramma's (M/V/X) 32 - 40 uur per week Ben jij een ervaren projectassistent die energie krijgt van organiseren, plannen en zorgen dat alles op rolletjes loopt? Wil jij bijdragen aan internationale jongerenprogramma’s die impact maken? Dan zijn wij op zoek naar jou! Wie zijn wij? De Anne Frank Stichting is een onafhankelijke organisatie die de plek beheert waar Anne Frank tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog was ondergedoken en waar zij haar dagboek schreef. De stichting brengt haar levensverhaal en haar werk wereldwijd onder de aandacht, mede ter bezinning op de gevaren van antisemitisme, racisme en discriminatie en het belang van vrijheid, gelijke rechten en democratie. Een van onze teams binnen onze afdeling Educatieve Projecten richt zich specifiek op jongeren van 16 tot 26 jaar. De kern hiervan is het Anne Frank Youth Network (AFYN), dat actief is in 20 landen. Jongeren worden hier opgeleid tot bruggenbouwers, organiseren dialoogbijeenkomsten en dragen lokaal én internationaal bij aan een sterke, weerbare en inclusieve democratische samenleving. Wat ga je doen als Project Assistent? Als project assistent binnen het team Jongeren ondersteun je op organisatorisch en administratief vlak diverse educatieve activiteiten voor en met jongeren. Jouw Belangrijkste Taken Praktisch organiseren van trainingen, bijeenkomsten, studiereizen en webinars (zowel nationaal als internationaal). Contact onderhouden met deelnemers (inclusief voorbereiding en nazorg). Verzorgen van de verspreiding van educatief materiaal, opstellen van deelnemerslijsten en beheren van de (financiële) projectadministratie. Notuleren van overleggen, verzorgen van correspondentie en het (digitaal) archiveren van documenten. Ondersteunen bij promotieactiviteiten en online communicatie. Wat breng jij mee? Opleiding & Ervaring: Minimaal 1 jaar relevante werkervaring in een ondersteunende of administratieve rol en een mbo denk- en werkniveau. Talenkennis: Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse taal (mondeling en schriftelijk) en goede kennis van de Engelse taal. Competenties: Je bent proactief, leergierig, hebt een echte hands-on mentaliteit en kunt nauwkeurig werken. Plannen & Organiseren: Je hebt uitstekende organisatorische skills, kunt goed prioriteiten stellen en schakelt makkelijk in een flexibele omgeving. Sociale skills: Je bent communicatief sterk en hebt affiniteit en enthousiasme in de omgang met jonge mensen. Je bent bekend met de activiteiten van de Anne Frank Stichting. Digitale vaardigheden: Affiniteit met social media (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp), online platformen (MS Teams, Zoom) en MS Office (Word, Excel). Je pikt nieuwe (interne) systemen snel op. Flexibiliteit: Je bent flexibel in je werktijden en incidenteel beschikbaar in het weekend. Wat bieden wij jou? Werken bij de Anne Frank Stichting betekent impact maken. Wij bieden een veelzijdige functie binnen een wereldberoemde organisatie met een belangrijke missie. Arbeidsvoorwaarden: Een afwisselende functie voor 32 tot 40 uur per week voor een jaar; bij goed functioneren verlenging tot 31 december 2028). Salaris: Een bruto maandsalaris van minimaal € 2.686,93 tot maximaal; 3.723,93 op basis van 38 uur (fulltime) en een royale eindejaarsuitkering van 6,3%. Goede balans: Een 40 (32)-urige werkweek met flexibele uren, een wekelijkse opbouw van 2 (1,2) ATV-uren en de mogelijkheid tot hybride werken. Werkplek: Een unieke en inspirerende werkplek in hartje Amsterdam. Extra’s: Uitstekende secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden, waaronder een bedrijfsfitnessregeling, fietsregeling en een ov-kaart voor je woon-werkverkeer.

review_candidates.location: Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
review_candidates.description: Property, construction and fit-out. Build the operating model of an AI-native built-environment business, from the inside, with the P&L to prove it. The opportunity Chin Hin Group is a diversified Malaysian group with listed businesses across the built-environment value chain. We are setting out to make our property, construction and fit-out businesses the most profitable in their markets, and EBITDA is the scoreboard. We are not hiring advisers to write that plan. We are hiring a small bench of senior operators who will own it: diagnose, decide, deploy and bank the result, with the Group's full transformation programme behind them. Why this is different from your current role You own the outcome, not the deck. The value you create shows up in P&Ls you can name, not in a steering-committee pack. Real tech, already in place. An integrated ERP backbone and an AI operating layer are live. You get to use them, not pitch for them. Proximity to power. You work directly with the Group Chief Transformation Officer and business CEOs, and present to ExCo. Decisions take weeks, not quarters. A launchpad. This bench feeds the Group's next generation of senior leaders. Role snapshot Title: Value Creation Partner / Principal Unit: Group Transformation Office Sector scope: Property development, construction, fit-out and interiors Reports to: Group Chief Transformation Officer, working day to day with business CEOs How you work: Small senior pods of 2–4, each leading one or two flagship value cases end to end The mandate Rebuild how money moves between design, procurement, site and handover, so that every ringgit of margin we plan is a ringgit we bank. In practice that means three shifts, each of which you will lead: From cost reporting to cost control. Bring best-in-class discipline to cost planning, tender and procurement: target costs locked at scheme design, variations governed, final accounts closed fast. From project heroics to project certainty. Install stage gates, earned value and cash forecasting so programme and margin risk is visible weeks earlier. From process plus AI to AI plus process. Redesign the work itself around the Group's ERP and AI layer: estimating, tender analysis, progress claims, site reporting and defects run as closed loops, with people handling the exceptions. What you will own Value agenda: Diagnose the value chain from land and feasibility to after-sales; identify where money is earned, lost, or left on the table, and build a ranked, Finance-signed pipeline of value cases. Commercial and cost: Lead target costing, value engineering, tender and package strategy, contract administration (PAM, CIDB, FIDIC) and group buying; protect where money is spent, committed, and recovered throughout the project lifecycle. Delivery certainty: Put stage gates, earned value and cash forecasting on flagship projects; push prefabrication and offsite where it pays to improve predictability and deliver to plan. EBITDA and cash: Turn each initiative into P&L and cash commitments with business CEOs; report monthly to ExCo and hold the business accountable for delivering and banking the results. AI and digital: Co-design closed-loop processes and AI agents with Group Digital & AI; process redesign comes before automation, enabling value creation initiatives to scale across the Group. Capability: Coach HODs and key users; leave playbooks and KPIs that hold after you move on, embedding lasting capability within the business. Who we are looking for You have been the person in the room who knew where the margin was hiding. You are deep in one of the three areas below and fluent in at least one other; we build each pod so that together it covers all three. Nobody is expected to have everything, and we value experience gained on the client, contractor, developer and advisory sides alike. What you get A competitive package , discussed in confidence with shortlisted candidates. A performance bonus of up to 12 months' salary . The amount is set by project performance: the EBITDA you verifiably deliver on the value cases you lead. Decision rights. Authority to stop, re-tender or re-scope within agreed limits, and direct access to ExCo to escalate the rest. The tools on day one. An integrated ERP backbone, an AI operating layer, and the Group Digital & AI team as your build partner. Exposure that compounds . A seat at the table where the Group decides how its businesses will run. Where this leads This bench is how the Group develops its next senior leaders. Strong performers can move into: Group Head of Value Creation Leadership roles in the Group's businesses A senior role with the potential to report directly to the Chairman Qualifications Professional standing preferred: RICS, RISM (BQSM-registered), CIOB, PMP, or CA/CFA for value-creation profiles. Degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Finance or Business is preferred but not required. Typically, 7–10 years for Principal and 10+ years for Partner, though a strong track record matters more than years served.
